reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about ordering, ensemble formation, and their impact on adsorption and selectivity, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the behavior of this specific septenary alloy under reaction conditions.
premises: Short-range atomic ordering can be increased by slow annealing vs rapid quenching in this alloy system.
Increased ordering creates defined active site ensembles.
Defined ensembles modify adsorption energies and activation barriers of ethanol oxidation intermediates.
Modified adsorption/barriers shift selectivity toward complete oxidation (CO2) over partial oxidation products.
These effects are separable from changes in surface area or composition.
